from_speaker: the pressure to use AI for everything
turning companies’ software stacks into slop
our_interpretation: Slop has the ordinary testable meaning of poorer software quality: more defects, unreliable operation, or avoidable maintenance and review burdens.
Some cases requires credible company-level examples, not an industry-wide average effect.
The causal assertion requires evidence connecting pressure to use AI with the degradation, rather than merely finding AI use and defects together.
In some cases limits the scope; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: At least one well-documented company case shows that organizational pressure to use AI contributed to a measurable deterioration in software quality or maintainability by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The alleged examples are shown not to involve deterioration or not to result from AI-use pressure, and sufficiently comprehensive evidence rules out the asserted cases. Successful adoption elsewhere alone cannot refute some cases.
